annotations.title: Leſt they ſhould be conuerted.
annotations.text: [1] Theſe ſpeaches here and els where, we muſt not ſo vnderſtand as though he ſpake in parables of purpoſe and to this end, that the hearers might not vnderſtand, leſt they ſhould be conuerted: which were as much to ſay as that he would not haue them vnderſtand, nor be conuerted: but we muſt learne the true ſenſe of this very place in S. Matthew [2] and in the Actes, [3]where our Sauiour and S. Paul ſpeake thus, They haue heard heauily, and haue ſhut their eies, leſt perhaps they may ſee, and vnderſtand, and be conuerted, and I heale them. Whereby it is euident, that the ſpeaking in parables vvas not the cauſe (for many beſide the Apoſtles heard and vnderſtood) but them ſelues would not heare, and vnderſtand, and be conuerted: and ſo were the cauſe of their owne wilful and obſtinate infidelity. And therfore alſo he ſpake in parables, becauſe they were not worthy to vnderſtand, as the other to whom he expounded them.

notes.text: God is not author of sinne, but mans owne will.

annotations.title: And ſleepe.
annotations.text: The Church, and Chriſts doctrine, (ſleepe vve, wake we) increaſeth by the great prouidence of God. only the preachers muſt ſow, and plant, and water, and <mn>◦</mn> God wil giue the increaſe, nouriſhing the ſeede in mens harts. And therfore we may not giue ouer, or be impatient and ſolicitous, if we haue not alwaies good ſucceſſe: but doing our duty, commit the reſt to God.

annotations.title: Muſtard ſeed.
annotations.text: ◦ If the Church and Truth had more and more decaied and been obſcured after the Apoſtles time vnto ours, as the Heretikes hold: then had it been great in the beginning, and ſmal afterward: where this Parable ſaith contrary, that it was a muſtard ſeed firſt, and afterward a great tree. vide Chrys. to. 5 contra Gentiles in vita S. Babylæ Mart.

annotations.title: The birdes.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Of al ſectes or doctrine, Chriſts religion at the beginning vvas the ſmalleſt, and moſt contemptible: but the ſucceſſe thereof farre paſſed al mans doctrine: in ſo much that afterward al the wiſeſt and greateſt of the world made their reſidence and reſt therein.
